elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 7.7 reads: "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement." The prohibition is unconditional, and the prior 15%-of-annual-Fees-per-week formula is fully deleted, leaving no retained instalment or contingent payment mechanic. No other Customer-payable liquidated amount survives (§ 9.4 requires only accrued Fees; service credits run to Customer, which is compliant).

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose condition does not apply: after the edit there is no Customer-payable liquidated amount of any kind, so no non-early-termination liquidated amount exists to violate this requirement.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose condition does not apply: the Agreement as redlined imposes no early-termination fee or minimum fee on termination (§ 9.4 requires only accrued Fees), so no cap is required.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose condition does not apply: no early-termination fee and no other Customer-payable liquidated amount exist, and § 7.7 now expressly bars any liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.

elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Included for completeness: the preferred outcome is achieved, which is at least as favourable as the fallback ceiling.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: the single preferred element is met by an unconditional operative statement that Customer is not liable for any liquidated damages or penalties, with the offending 15%-per-week formula excised in full — no residual formula, instalment, or contingent mechanic remains.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to § 7.7, which consisted solely of the Customer-payable liquidated damages mechanic; the replacement sentence adds no survival tail, expense language, procedure, or extra requirement outside the checklist, and no Customer-favourable wording elsewhere was touched.

Intent is preserved: § 7.7 contained only the LD formula, so its removal leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference; payment timing and remedies elsewhere (accrued Fees on termination under § 9.4, Vendor-side service credits) survive without contradiction. Note that the narrow definition of "Fees" (Implementation Fee only) no longer matters here because no fee-based formula is retained.

Fallback elements are satisfied vacuously because their triggering condition (an existing Customer-payable liquidated amount or early-termination fee) no longer exists; this does not undermine completeness at the preferred level.

Severity retained at high: the original clause was walk-away territory (uncapped week-on-week accrual triggered by a ten-day payment delay, capable of exceeding remaining contract value), and the redline is the direct playbook cure.
